agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager sees a candidate who writes and enforces procedures for hazardous work and openly admits the GMP gap, which may earn a phone screen, but nothing concrete shows plant-readiness.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the unsupported 'cut training time in half' claim, but it adds details the brief doesn't give, such as new teachers being 'experienced professionals' and students handling 'acids, open flames and glassware.'

works_the_facts.reason: Figures are restated rather than derived: it never adds up roughly 1,000 student-years without a serious injury since 2019, about 24 hours a year (around 170 hours total) of adult training, or the 17-point (about 41% relative) rise in the AP pass rate.

right_comparison.reason: It compares teacher onboarding to plant onboarding reasonably, but it doesn't confront the real alternative, a candidate who already has GMP experience, beyond admitting the gap.

qualification.reason: The GMP and LMS hedge is only 'I expect to learn' and 'will learn,' with no named course, timeline or checkable milestone the reader could hold the applicant to.

objections.reason: It meets the 'teachers don't understand regulated plants' objection head-on and frames procedure discipline as transferable, but the answer stays general and offers no evidence of preparation for GMP.

fit.reason: It is a conventional one-page cover letter in a suitable register, though it leaves out the time-halving claim the user asked for (defensibly, since nothing supports it) without flagging that.
